9.speaker: Narrator
9.text: Walter lit his cigar and took a few drags before continuing.

10.speaker: Walter Tusk
10.text: “The consensus is that we see eye to eye in the economic direction you have taken by promoting a market economy.”

11.speaker: Walter Tusk
11.text: “Many in the group are disappointed in the economic direction that you took by promoting an inefficient planned economy.”

12.speaker: Player
12.text: “I'm glad that the group is supportive.”

13.speaker: Player
13.text: “What can be done to amend the situation?”

14.speaker: Player
14.text: “Promises made during the election had to be upheld. That was the main reason behind the decision.”

15.speaker: Player
15.text: “The opinions of the Lotherberg group don't concern me. I will make choices on my own accord.”

16.speaker: Walter Tusk
16.text: “If the administration were to pass a private corporation tax cut and privatise both healthcare and education, it would do wonders in the attitude of Lotherberg towards the administration.”

17.speaker: Walter Tusk
17.text: “Dissatisfaction of Lotherberg should concern you, Mr. President. It should concern you very much. Especially after you took our 'contribution' and didn't act on it.”

18.speaker: Walter Tusk
18.text: “They represent a large collective of economic power. Cooperation would be helpful in solving the recession.”

20.speaker: Walter Tusk
20.text: “Political motivations are admirable but economics is about numbers and the current reality, not the past.”

22.speaker: Player
22.text: “I will give large private corporations a tax reduction.” [Promise Tax Cut]

23.speaker: Player
23.text: “I will make tax decisions objectively. Can't promise you anything.”

24.speaker: Walter Tusk
24.text: “I'm very satisfied to hear this. To us and the prosperous future of Sordland!”

25.speaker: Walter Tusk
25.text: “Oh let's not be hasty. The recession will end if Lotherberg is on your side, President.”

27.speaker: Player
27.text: “Maybe meeting in the middle is the solution.”

28.speaker: Player
28.text: “This time it isn't. I won't change my mind.”

31.speaker: Narrator
31.text: Walter left and Serge came to pick me up.

35.speaker: Walter Tusk
35.text: “It seems that you have decided to tackle the Old Guard in the new Constitution. That is brave indeed.”

36.speaker: Walter Tusk
36.text: "We are really concerned about the state of emergency. We found ourselves worrying about the future."

37.speaker: Walter Tusk
37.text: “Finally a President that listens to the people. It won't be easy to pass the new Constitution through the Assembly and the Supreme Court.”

38.speaker: Walter Tusk
38.text: "We could be a strong ally in breaking that status quo, if you fulfil our requests. We can help with the Assembly and perhaps the Court..."

39.speaker: Walter Tusk
39.text: “We could help you get it through, if you in return help us with a few economic requests.”

40.speaker: Walter Tusk
40.text: “We need stability for business to function. So if you want us on your side with our capital there are a few requests on our end.”

47.speaker: Walter Tusk
47.text: “We had a deal about the first mega infrastructure project.”

48.speaker: Walter Tusk
48.text: “You rejected our previous discrete offer to pick Underhall Construction for the execution of the first mega infrastructure project.”
48.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Relations_Walter_Promise_Company"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Turn01_InT_Investment_Highway"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn01_InT_Investment_Railway"] == true)

49.speaker: Walter Tusk
49.text: “You held on to that promise and awarded the contract to Underhall Construction. This went well in our book.”

50.speaker: Walter Tusk
50.text: “You broke that promise and didn't award the contract to Underhall Construction. This action led to a huge disappointment in the Group.”

51.speaker: Walter Tusk
51.text: “However, you still made the right choice. Your party not getting that donation is unfortunate though. Why someone wouldn't want that money is beyond me.”

52.speaker: Walter Tusk
52.text: “We are aware of the upcoming tax meeting and it would be a step in the right direction if private corporations would get a tax cut.”

53.speaker: Walter Tusk
53.text: “To boost the economy with job creation, of course... And the positive side effect would be our support to the administration throughout the entire term.”

54.speaker: Walter Tusk
54.text: “Usually the Lotherberg spokesman doesn't directly comment on the administration, but I'd like to say a few things since this was a special evening.”

58.speaker: Walter Tusk
58.text: “This action led to disappointment in the Group.”

59.speaker: Walter Tusk
59.text: “From our end the previous mishap would be cleared and confidence in the new administration from the business community would be restored.”

60.speaker: Player
60.text: “I'm interested to collaborate further in our shared interests.”

61.speaker: Player
61.text: “I will give a private corporation tax cut and enable privatization in health and education.” [Promise Tax Cut]

62.speaker: Player
62.text: “I will make tax and privatization decisions objectively. Can't promise you anything.”

65.speaker: Walter Tusk
65.text: “Privatization can lead to a many good things, President Rayne. It is certainly an opportunity to raise further money inside the welfare branches.”

69.speaker: Narrator
69.text: He gestured at the guards and then called me inside the small VIP lounge.

70.speaker: Narrator
70.text: He called me inside the small VIP lounge.

72.speaker: Walter Tusk
72.text: “Either way... President, we are here and always ready to work with you if you change your mind. Don't forget that.”

73.speaker: Player
73.text: “[Request Bribe] I would want a financial contribution from your end.”

74.speaker: Player
74.text: “We are certainly interested in maintaining a good relationship with Lotherberg.”

75.speaker: Player
75.text: “Good to know but not sure how this concerns me.”

76.speaker: Player
76.text: “We don't share similar interests with Lotherberg.”

79.speaker: Walter Tusk
79.text: “In that case we can move towards a better future together.”

80.speaker: Walter Tusk
80.text: “Yet we live in the same country don't we? Let's settle our differences.”

81.speaker: Narrator
81.text: He looked me in the eye.

82.speaker: Walter Tusk
82.text: “There are many who put their trust in you.”

83.speaker: Player
83.text: “I will think about it but not now.”

84.speaker: Player
84.text: “There is nothing to work together on. Good evening.”

85.speaker: Player
85.text: “It is assuring to know that we are allies.”

86.speaker: Player
86.text: “Glad we could come to an agreement, Walter.”

87.speaker: Walter Tusk
87.text: “The last time obviously caused some trust issues between us. We would love to contribute in the future if you agree to the terms.”

88.speaker: Walter Tusk
88.text: “That's a shame. I did offer you a peace branch.”

89.speaker: Walter Tusk
89.text: “Why can't we all just be friends?”

90.speaker: Player
90.text: “I don't think so, I have other plans for the economy.”

91.speaker: Player
91.text: "Maybe we can. I'll see what I can do."

96.speaker: Walter Tusk
96.text: “The group wants a private corporation tax cut and privatization in healthcare and education.”

97.speaker: Walter Tusk
97.text: “The only thing the Group wants is a private corporation tax cut and we will fully support your administration.”

100.speaker: Player
100.text: “I will give a private corporation tax cut and enable privatization in health and education.” [Promise Tax Cut]

101.speaker: Player
101.text: “That is too much of an ask. On third thought, I have to reject.”

102.speaker: Player
102.text: “I will pass a private corporation tax cut.” [Promise Tax Cut]

103.speaker: Player
103.text: “That is too much of an ask. On third thought, I have to reject.”

106.speaker: Narrator
106.text: We were in Lachaven to work with the Business Council to assess weaknesses in the economy. Symon organised a dinner with the affluent economic figureheads of Sordland.

110.speaker: Narrator
110.text: Beaming with pride, he led us to a private room and got us seated at a large table, covered for the occasion with a maroon tablecloth.

111.speaker: Narrator
111.text: When we arrived, the streets were quiet and police forces were patrolling everywhere. The emergency was felt in the vacant city.

112.speaker: Narrator
112.text: When we arrived, the streets were bustling with activity even though the atmosphere in the country was tense. Lachaveners didn't seem very worried.

113.speaker: Narrator
113.text: Together with Walter Tusk, Edith Agnoc, Mikail Aven and Symon Holl, we entered the renowned Esteria restaurant by the coast.

114.speaker: Narrator
114.text: A short blonde man whose embroidered pocket read "Manager," greeted us and waved his arms in excitement as he told us how pleased he was to have us in his establishment.

115.speaker: Narrator
115.text: We were quickly served by a group of servers. Walter spoke as they started taking our orders.

116.speaker: Walter Tusk
116.text: “I recommend the Lachaven Salmon, President. You have to taste this local delicacy here, the best in Sordland."

117.speaker: Symon Holl
117.text: "No need for that. I hope everybody enjoys the evening."

118.speaker: Player
118.text: “Don't get me wrong, Mr. Tusk, but of course I've tasted this greatness many times here already.

122.speaker: Walter Tusk
122.text: “I recommend the Lachaven Salmon of this place, President. I know that you're from Lachaven, but I bet you haven't tasted anything like this before."

125.speaker: Player
125.text: “I appreciate the advice but I don't like salmon."

127.speaker: Walter Tusk
127.text: “Really? Too bad. I guess that's your loss."

128.speaker: Walter Tusk
128.text: “Excuse me, President. I should have known that a man of your calibre would be a regular at Esteria."

133.speaker: Walter Tusk
133.text: "You should couple that dish with some Lespian salad, President. It's no good when it's by itself."

134.speaker: Walter Tusk
134.text: "That's two starch dishes, President. That's no good."

138.speaker: Narrator
138.text: The servers placed glasses in front of each of us and served bread and water. After they were done taking orders, they quickly left us alone in the private room.

140.speaker: Player
140.text: "You're right. I'll get some salad too."

141.speaker: Player
141.text: "Why don't you focus on your own order, Mr. Tusk?"

142.speaker: Player
142.text: "Why don't you focus on your own order, Mr. Tusk?"

145.speaker: Narrator
145.text: One of the servers quickly jumped in the conversation and told me that Mr. Tusk was right, and went on to explain why two starch dishes do not go together. He then offered to prepare me something special.

146.speaker: Walter Tusk
146.text: "It was just a suggestion, President... Come now, relax."

147.speaker: Walter Tusk
147.text: "I only wanted you to have the best possible experience!"

150.speaker: Player
150.text: "No, I want exactly what I ordered."

152.speaker: Player
152.text: "What is this? Can't I order what I want anymore?"

153.speaker: Walter Tusk
153.text: "Oh come on. He is the President! Serve him what he wants!"

154.speaker: Narrator
154.text: The server looked uneasy. He replied, "I'm sorry, Mr. President. This is a very special establishment and we want to provide the best quality service. Therefore, we cannot serve two starch dishes as they do not complement each ot-"

155.speaker: Narrator
155.text: The server respectfully bowed his head and took notes.

156.speaker: Narrator
156.text: After a brief argument, the server agreed to prepare my order and apologized.

157.speaker: Edith Agnoc
157.text: “Mr. President, I didn't have the possibility to thank you for coming today. Your presence means a great deal."

158.speaker: Mikail Aven
158.text: "Indeed, sir. It's an honor to dine with you."

160.speaker: Player
160.text: "It's great to be here with the members of the Business Council."

162.speaker: Mikail Aven
162.text: "We should thank Symon for organizing this meeting."

163.speaker: Walter Tusk
163.text: "Well, it tastes even better! Best of Lespia, the Chateau de Falenco 1934."

165.speaker: Narrator
165.text: Symon gestured at the expensive looking red wine bottle that one of the servers had just brought to the table.

170.speaker: Symon Holl
170.text: "Do you want some, sir? It is Chateau de Falenco, from 1934."

171.speaker: Walter Tusk
171.text: "Are you serious, Mr. Rayne? Are you going to pass on a Chateau de Falenco 1934?"

172.speaker: Player
172.text: "What kind of question is that? Of course."

174.speaker: Player
174.text: "Thank you, but I'm not going to drink this evening."

175.speaker: Player
175.text: "I'd prefer something regional or at least Sordish."

178.speaker: Narrator
178.text: After filling everybody's glasses, Symon stood up and raised his glass.

179.speaker: Player
179.text: "As I've said, I'm not going to drink."

180.speaker: Player
180.text: "Fine... I can't turn down a man like you, Mr. Tusk."

181.speaker: Player
181.text: "I can't drink now when the country is suffering."

182.speaker: Narrator
182.text: He laughed and gestured at the waiter to bring the best Sordish wine that they had.

184.speaker: Narrator
184.text: The waiter brought a bottle of 'Dandelion.' The world famous red wine from Borin. Symon went ahead and grabbed the bottle from the waiter. He poured some in my glass and waited for me to taste it before filling it up.

192.speaker: Walter Tusk
192.text: "But don't you think you overreacted with this emergency situation?"

194.speaker: Narrator
194.text: There was a brief silence at the table before Symon cut in.

196.speaker: Narrator
196.text: After everybody was served their preferred drinks, Symon stood up with his glass raised.

197.speaker: Symon Holl
197.text: "I'd like to raise a toast to all of you here today."

198.speaker: Symon Holl
198.text: "We will get through this period as well."

199.speaker: Symon Holl
199.text: "We're meeting here tonight in difficult times. But I believe that, with hard work, cooperation and trust..."

200.speaker: Symon Holl
200.text: "I'd like to thank Mr. Rayne again for his decisiveness when it comes to economic policies... I'm sure we will stop this recession."

201.speaker: Symon Holl
201.text: "I also thank Mr. Tusk for being here with us today... His presence is an honor."

202.speaker: Symon Holl
202.text: "And of course, my colleagues from the Business Council, Mrs. Agnoc and Mr. Aven. Without you, none of these would have been possible."

203.speaker: Symon Holl
203.text: "Let's drink to future cooperation and growth."

205.speaker: Narrator
205.text: Everybody raised their glasses and toasted each other.

206.speaker: Narrator
206.text: After a couple of more minutes, the servers arrived with our meals.

207.speaker: Narrator
207.text: When I tasted the food, I went back to my past. It reminded me of my childhood in this city. Even though I couldn't recall much about my father, I remembered that he also loved the food of Esteria.

211.speaker: Narrator
211.text: The food tasted amazing. Walter was right, this place must have been the best place in all of Lachaven.

212.speaker: Edith Agnoc
212.text: "So, how did you find the food of the best fine dining restaurant in Lachaven, Mr. President?"

213.speaker: Player
213.text: “This can't get old. It's an experience. The chef must be tipped.”

214.speaker: Walter Tusk
214.text: "Definitely it doesn't. But I will take care of the tip. Don't you worry.”

215.speaker: Mikail Aven
215.text: "Tipping is no small thing. I actually don't like giving tips. People have salaries for a reason.”

216.speaker: Player
216.text: “Fine food is like fine art. But this particular one is a masterpiece.”

218.speaker: Edith Agnoc
218.text: "I know exactly what you mean. Art is something else, it embodies so much about us and the world surrounding our lives. And food ca-"

220.speaker: Walter Tusk
220.text: “Says the man visiting one of the finest restaurants in Sordland.”

221.speaker: Walter Tusk
221.text: "There is an art of everything. The art of making money, food, wine and love."

222.speaker: Edith Agnoc
222.text: “Always generous when it comes to small things.”

223.speaker: Edith Agnoc
223.text: “Don't blame it on him. Mr. President didn't choose the place."

224.speaker: Player
224.text: “Not a big fan of fancy food, but I must admit that it's very tasty.”

226.speaker: Player
226.text: "No, I loved it. I just don't like this luxurious fine dining culture."

227.speaker: Player
227.text: "I liked it but it is nothing special."

229.speaker: Walter Tusk
229.text: "I hope the manager did not hear that."

230.speaker: Mikail Aven
230.text: "How are things going in the Maroon Palace? The pressure must have increased after you attended that funeral."

232.speaker: Mikail Aven
232.text: "How are things going in the Maroon Palace? The pressure must have increased after you did not attend that funeral."

233.speaker: Player
233.text: "The pressure was already high. Not much has changed."

234.speaker: Player
234.text: "It did. But it was the right decision."

235.speaker: Player
235.text: "I have to say, the future is looking good."

239.speaker: Player
239.text: "It's tough but our work on the new constitution continues."

240.speaker: Player
240.text: "It's tough but the new laws will fix it."

241.speaker: Narrator
241.text: We were escorted by heavily armed police forces as well as the presidential guard.

243.speaker: Mikail Aven
243.text: "Of course. I didn't mean to criticise your decision."

246.speaker: Narrator
246.text: As we conversed with Mikail, I heard Walter raise his voice in an apparent argument with Edith and Symon. We both stopped to listen.

247.speaker: Walter Tusk
247.text: "...Arcasia knows the right way of doing business. Their approach to the world is real and raw. I'd prefer that cutthroat approach in comparison to the niceties."

248.speaker: Symon Holl
248.text: "I mean... It's a nice country to visit too. I have travelled there often in business trips. Their attitude on-"

251.speaker: Edith Agnoc
251.text: "All countries are nice to visit if you have the cash."

252.speaker: Walter Tusk
252.text: "Why would you, President? Or why wouldn't you?"

253.speaker: Mikail Aven
253.text: "Where is this pile of gold you keep talking about Walter?"

255.speaker: Player
255.text: “Make sure to lay a good foundation for our negotiations to start on.”

256.speaker: Player
256.text: “I am looking forward to those visits. It's been a long time since I left the country.”

257.speaker: Symon Holl
257.text: “Walter is taking us down the rabbit hole again.”

258.speaker: Symon Holl
258.text: “Our talented team is lead by Mr. Wisci. His wealth of knowledge and extensive connections will aid in our endeavour.”

259.speaker: Player
259.text: “Money does turn the world around. Travel is the least you can buy with it.”

260.speaker: Symon Holl
260.text: “Staalport is a relatively calm and nice seaside city. I'm sure you'll like it there.”

261.speaker: Walter Tusk
261.text: “The picture would have been very different.”

262.speaker: Player
262.text: "Exactly. How about the people who don't have extra cash to spend?"

264.speaker: Mikail Aven
264.text: "Can't disagree. The President deserves a better wage."

265.speaker: Symon Holl
265.text: “Walter is taking us down the rabbit hole again.”

266.speaker: Player
266.text: “Old men plant trees whose shade they shall never sit under.”

268.speaker: Player
268.text: “Truly an egotistical way to look at the world.”

269.speaker: Walter Tusk
269.text: “What about disease? What about death? What about everything that is wrong with the world?”

270.speaker: Player
270.text: “You are right, Walter. We only live once.”

271.speaker: Walter Tusk
271.text: "You work day and night for the nation, surely you deserve a higher salary."

272.speaker: Walter Tusk
272.text: “Half the globe isn't worth our time nor attention. That won't change unless profitability increases.”

273.speaker: Walter Tusk
273.text: "As long as you hold the treasure the country is yours. We are all part of that treasure."

277.speaker: Walter Tusk
277.text: “These are matters beyond our lives. We should focus on the betterment of ourselves and enjoy what we have, instead of worrying about what others don't have.”

278.speaker: Mikail Aven
278.text: “Walter's classic absolutes. But I do agree with you investment-wise. There are only a select group of countries that guarantee a return on investment.”

280.speaker: Player
280.text: “I am not a person to be motivated or influenced by money.”

281.speaker: Walter Tusk
281.text: “There we go! You have to let loose of that burden of yours or it will consume you.”

282.speaker: Symon Holl
282.text: “Talking of which, we are preparing our visit to Agnolia and Wehlen where we will meet their governments to settle our trade negotiations.”

283.speaker: Walter Tusk
283.text: "We see eye to eye! What a privilege to agree with the President of Sordland himself."

284.speaker: Walter Tusk
284.text: “It's just facts. Life is short and there is only so much we can do. Why not focus all the energy on ourselves?”

285.speaker: Walter Tusk
285.text: “An idealist at heart. You know what they say, being a romantic idealist is easy when you have the time and money to be able to just sit down, relax and dream.”

286.speaker: Walter Tusk
286.text: “You would be surprised how much it is so, it is but a matter of price.”

287.speaker: Walter Tusk
287.text: “Yet rulers always use their treasure to maintain power. If you did not control the Ministry of Economy or the Central Bank...”

292.speaker: Walter Tusk
292.text: “Last time I went somewhere for that sort of thing was at university. And even then we had our wild times thanks to Konrath's connected entourage. Also-”

293.speaker: Mikail Aven
293.text: “It certainly depends on what you are looking for. Cultural tourism doesn't require a fancy hotel.”

300.speaker: Mikail Aven
300.text: "I have to congratulate Mr. Rayne for starting such a massive project."

310.speaker: Mikail Aven
310.text: "I saw that Underhall Construction has already started with the highway construction."
310.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Turn02_InT_Corporation_UnderhallConstruction"] == true) and (Variable["BaseGame.Turn01_InT_Investment_Highway"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn01_InT_Investment_Railway"] == true) and (Variable["BaseGame.Turn01_InT_Investment_Highway"] == true)

311.speaker: Mikail Aven
311.text: "Hopefully that project will bring new investments from Agnolia. The mood is already becoming positive."

312.speaker: Mikail Aven
312.text: "I saw that the construction of the highway has already started. I have my concerns about the company, but I hope they do a good job."
312.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn02_InT_Corporation_UnderhallConstruction"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Turn01_InT_Investment_Highway"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn01_InT_Investment_Railway"] == true) and (Variable["BaseGame.Turn01_InT_Investment_Highway"] == true)

313.speaker: Mikail Aven
313.text: "I expect that the project will bring new investments from Agnolia. The mood is already becoming positive."

314.speaker: Mikail Aven
314.text: "I saw that Underhall Construction has already started with the railway construction."
314.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Turn02_InT_Corporation_UnderhallConstruction"] == true) and (Variable["BaseGame.Turn01_InT_Investment_Highway"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn01_InT_Investment_Railway"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn01_InT_Investment_Highway"] == true) == false)

315.speaker: Mikail Aven
315.text: "That project will surely boost our economy. The mood is already very positive."

316.speaker: Mikail Aven
316.text: "I saw that the construction of the railway has already started. I have my concerns about the company, but I hope they do a good job."
316.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn02_InT_Corporation_UnderhallConstruction"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Turn01_InT_Investment_Highway"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn01_InT_Investment_Railway"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn01_InT_Investment_Highway"] == true) == false)

317.speaker: Mikail Aven
317.text: "That project will surely boost our economy if done correctly. The mood is already becoming positive."

318.speaker: Mikail Aven
318.text: "The business bailout package was a great investment. I have already seen some positive results."
318.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_EconomicRelief_BailedBusinesses"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn01_InT_Investment_Highway"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn01_InT_Investment_Railway"] == true) == false)

319.speaker: Narrator
319.text: Symon poured some wine in my glass and waited for me to taste it before filling it up.

324.speaker: Narrator
324.text: The taste of the wine was immediately stimulating and delightful to my palate. It immediately reminded me of our visits to my father's vineyard when I was a little kid.

325.speaker: Narrator
325.text: The wine's sweet and bitter flavours exploded in my mouth. The aroma of gooseberries and lilacs tumbled across my tongue, and my mouth tingled with them long after I'd swallowed.

327.speaker: Narrator
327.text: Honestly, it tasted like any other wine.

328.speaker: Symon Holl
328.text: "How is it? Is the taste to your liking?"

329.speaker: Player
329.text: "It tastes like heaven. Reminds me of my father's vineyard."

330.speaker: Symon Holl
330.text: "How is it? Is the taste to your liking?"

331.speaker: Player
331.text: "Fine balance and a nice touch of gooseberries... I like it."

332.speaker: Player
332.text: "It has a sour and delicate vegetal character. Is it Arcasia I'm tasting?"

336.speaker: Player
336.text: "Thank you for your support, Mr. Aven."

337.speaker: Player
337.text: "No need for that, Mr. Aven. The State is just doing its job."

338.speaker: Player
338.text: "I hope the investment returns will be great."

339.speaker: Mikail Aven
339.text: "It has already saved many businesses from declaring bankruptcy."

340.speaker: Mikail Aven
340.text: "I have to congratulate Mr. Rayne for spending a massive amount of money for the businesses. This sets a good atmosphere for trust."

345.speaker: Mikail Aven
345.text: "The relief package was also a great investment. It has already saved many businesses from declaring bankruptcy."

346.speaker: Mikail Aven
346.text: "I have to congratulate Mr. Rayne for such major projects."

347.speaker: Mikail Aven
347.text: "I've heard that you've bought a new villa, Symon."
347.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_EconomicRelief_BailedBusinesses"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn01_InT_Investment_Highway"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn01_InT_Investment_Railway"] == true) == false)

349.speaker: Symon Holl
349.text: “I don't comment on rumours, but I'll make an exception since we are among friends. It's true.”

350.speaker: Player
350.text: “You are doing a great job so you deserve it.”

351.speaker: Player
351.text: “A new villa is a bit much. Especially in this economy when people are suffering.”

352.speaker: Player
352.text: “Maybe it shows overcompensation somewhat. Everybody is free to do whatever they want.”

353.speaker: Walter Tusk
353.text: “Where there is demand there is supply. The market rules supreme as always.”

354.speaker: Symon Holl
354.text: “It is a small seaside villa at the outskirts of Conriat. It's just a modest house with a swimming pool and a small golf course in the property."

355.speaker: Walter Tusk
355.text: “So what? My car collection is nearing the forty mark. They are all old timer models.”

356.speaker: Edith Agnoc
356.text: “He *is* one of the hardest working ministers in the government. He has surely deserved it.”

358.speaker: Player
358.text: “Rewards give the motivation to ensure people go that extra mile.”

359.speaker: Walter Tusk
359.text: “But talking about rewards... It is a fact that the government pays far less than the private sector.”

360.speaker: Player
360.text: “Great city to buy real estate in. Conriat is seeing a surge of investments.”

361.speaker: Player
361.text: "So you're becoming a neighbour to Marcel Koronti?"

362.speaker: Edith Agnoc
362.text: “Underhall Construction made a fortune constructing houses there.”

363.speaker: Walter Tusk
363.text: “Don't expect the rich to become modest in the near future. That would be a pipe dream.”

364.speaker: Symon Holl
364.text: “That's true but that was a change made on purpose to push for improvements from the inside.”

365.speaker: Player
365.text: “I always advocate against ostentatious behaviour. Money shouldn't be wasted for luxury."

367.speaker: Player
367.text: “Some prefer the carrot and stick approach. I'm more result oriented.”

369.speaker: Symon Holl
369.text: "You may be tasting the oak from the barrels, or maybe its the gooseberries. It's definitely not Arcasia, Mr. President."

371.speaker: Walter Tusk
371.text: "What? This wine doesn't even need testing."

372.speaker: Symon Holl
372.text: "Should I fill your glass or would you want another drink, sir?"

373.speaker: Player
373.text: "I think I'm good. I won't have anything for now."

375.speaker: Walter Tusk
375.text: "I've heard that he was a big wine connoisseur. May he rest in peace."

376.speaker: Walter Tusk
376.text: "You know your wine, Mr. Rayne. I respect that."

379.speaker: Player
379.text: "Honestly, I was never close to him. I can't recall too much apart from his lavish parties."

383.speaker: Narrator
383.text: He grabbed the bottle again to pour some into Walter Tusk's glass.

384.speaker: Walter Tusk
384.text: "You didn't have to serve us, Mr. Holl. There are servers around here."

389.speaker: Narrator
389.text: Several of the heavily armed guards were also inside with us, protecting every entrance and exit.

393.speaker: Narrator
393.text: The guards bowed their heads and went outside. Walter sighed in relief.

394.speaker: Narrator
394.text: As all of us started eating. Walter stopped and looked at the guards before turning to me.

395.speaker: Walter Tusk
395.text: "I know that we are in a state of emergency, Mr. Rayne. But can't we even eat alone?"

396.speaker: Walter Tusk
396.text: "What are they protecting here? They have already surrounded the whole restaurant."

397.speaker: Player
397.text: "It is a necessity, Mr. Tusk. There's nothing I can do about it."

398.speaker: Player
398.text: "They have to be prepared for everything."

399.speaker: Player
399.text: "I can take them out, if you want, Mr. Tusk."

400.speaker: Player
400.text: "You're right. Can you guys leave us alone here, please?"

402.speaker: Player
402.text: "Can you guys leave us alone here, please?"

404.speaker: Player
404.text: "Please leave the room. You scared Mr. Tusk."

406.speaker: Narrator
406.text: He didn't look too pleased about the whole situation.

407.speaker: Mikail Aven
407.text: "We all hope so, Mr. President. But I think it will work out."

409.speaker: Mikail Aven
409.text: "Mr. Holl also deserves credit, of course. Our *great* economy minister..."

411.speaker: Mikail Aven
411.text: "Why? I thought you said you were great at economy."

414.speaker: Player
414.text: "Modest? Are you being sarcastic with me?"

415.speaker: Edith Agnoc
415.text: "I've heard that your father was a very wealthy man."

422.speaker: Narrator
422.text: Edith, who was sitting to my left, gently put her hand over my arm for a few seconds.

423.speaker: Walter Tusk
423.text: "A correction. It wasn't his policies that destroyed him. It was the Old Guard."
423.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Autocrat_Path"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Autocrat_Path"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn03_EnT_Business_GuardsOutside"] == true)

424.speaker: Player
424.text: "The kid can handle himself. He doesn't need anybody else.”

426.speaker: Edith Agnoc
426.text: "I've heard that you had a difficult life in Deyr. Is that right?"

427.speaker: Walter Tusk
427.text: "That's a good choice. Having a degree in Sordland separates you from the rabble. And we especially need more people who understand economics."

428.speaker: Edith Agnoc
428.text: "I've heard that you were brought up in the capital and experienced all the power shift as it happened. Is that right? It must have been tough."

429.speaker: Mikail Aven
429.text: "But I agree that we need more economists to enter politics. It's unfortunate that Ewald Alphonso was the only leader who actually studied economics.”

430.speaker: Player
430.text: "My childhood was very difficult. But it definitely made me stronger."

431.speaker: Player
431.text: “My family cared for me as much as they could. I couldn't ask for more than that.”

432.speaker: Player
432.text: “I try to leave my past behind and focus on today. It's who we have become that matters.”

433.speaker: Mikail Aven
433.text: “Walter stop with the conspiracy theories. I think we've had enough drinks.”

434.speaker: Mikail Aven
434.text: “Talking of which, it's great that we have another leader who actually studied economics and understands it. Like Mr. Alphonso."

435.speaker: Walter Tusk
435.text: “He threatened their economic power base over the country through a vast privatization plan. They removed him and backed you after.”

436.speaker: Mikail Aven
436.text: “True, but I think it was his ambition that brought him down. Too many big changes in a short time frame.”

440.speaker: Mikail Aven
440.text: “That's what I say after a good night of drinking.”

441.speaker: Player
441.text: “I always had a gut feeling about his sudden fall.”

442.speaker: Walter Tusk
442.text: “Sometimes it impacts people more negatively. My father used to beat me up good when I crossed the line.”

443.speaker: Player
443.text: "Of course it was. They are a big threat."

446.speaker: Symon Holl
446.text: “I never met your family, Mr. President. How are they doing, if you don't mind me asking?”

447.speaker: Player
447.text: “Look at what he caused. Studying doesn't get you to the finish line.”

448.speaker: Edith Agnoc
448.text: “We are here because of him. I don't think we had a chance, if he hadn't screwed up.”

449.speaker: Player
449.text: "We don't talk much since I became President."

450.speaker: Mikail Aven
450.text: "It can happen. Sometimes work can get in the way. Don't stress yourself over it."

451.speaker: Mikail Aven
451.text: "Well, the rascal didn't even ask for permission to use the yacht and just took it. He basically stole it..."

452.speaker: Player
452.text: "I prefer not to talk about my family."

453.speaker: Player
453.text: “We are in this mess because of him. His political failure nearly destroyed us.”

454.speaker: Player
454.text: "He is going through the teenager period. It's difficult to connect with him, he's a little shy."

455.speaker: Player
455.text: "Mikail. What did you just say to me?"

456.speaker: Player
456.text: “Alphonso was an inspiration for all reformists."

457.speaker: Mikail Aven
457.text: “Wish that was my son's biggest problem...”

458.speaker: Edith Agnoc
458.text: "Darron seemed to be doing fine. I saw that his yacht party in Benfi made the local news."

459.speaker: Mikail Aven
459.text: “He was, he truly wanted to transform this country to a modern nation. His term was very difficult though. He got destroyed.”

460.speaker: Walter Tusk
460.text: “Family is everything. My advice would be to make sure that Franc has a solid relationship with you. He is your future, after all."

461.speaker: Edith Agnoc
461.text: "I said that about my daughter too. And she dropped out of university..."

462.speaker: Player
462.text: “I'm trying my best to be a good father to him. He seems to be somewhat introverted.”

464.speaker: Player
464.text: "Some people are more sensible. I believe balance is possible."

465.speaker: Player
465.text: "The gap between the rich and the poor is the root cause of this."

466.speaker: Symon Holl
466.text: “Some of us are more sensible than others. Balance is possible.”

468.speaker: Symon Holl
468.text: "I already had my eye on the area. Plus it wasn't intended to be public."

469.speaker: Edith Agnoc
469.text: "Come on, let's not talk about finance or politics for now. We came here to relax."

470.speaker: Walter Tusk
470.text: "I'm just saying that he's free to do what he please with his hard earned money."

472.speaker: Symon Holl
472.text: "Not really. His place is very remote."

473.speaker: Walter Tusk
473.text: "Conriat has a way of pulling certain people in, it seems."

475.speaker: Walter Tusk
475.text: "Oh come on! Leave the man be, President."

477.speaker: Narrator
477.text: She turned to Walter and Symon.

478.speaker: Narrator
478.text: They nodded at her and took a sip from their drinks. She slightly leaned towards me.

479.speaker: Edith Agnoc
479.text: "So, Mr. Rayne, why don't you tell us what's behind that strong character of yours?"

480.speaker: Player
480.text: "It didn't contribute much. My success has nothing to do with that."

481.speaker: Edith Agnoc
481.text: “Would you say that it contributed a lot to your success?"

482.speaker: Player
482.text: "It was difficult times in the capital. But I've learned a lot about politics."

483.speaker: Player
483.text: "I didn't suffer much thanks to my family. We didn't have much but we were stable."

485.speaker: Player
485.text: "It certainly helped. Money opened a lot of doors."

486.speaker: Player
486.text: "We had money but we weren't happy. I learned a lot about life thanks to my absent father."

487.speaker: Walter Tusk
487.text: "Of course not. You've worked hard for it. After all, money can't buy diligence."

488.speaker: Walter Tusk
488.text: "Of course it did. What kind of question is that, Edith?"

490.speaker: Player
490.text: "They're doing great. We have no problems."

492.speaker: Symon Holl
492.text: "That's great to hear. Your son must be very proud of you."

493.speaker: Walter Tusk
493.text: “Family is everything. My advice would be to make sure that Franc has a solid relationship with you. He is your future, after all."

494.speaker: Player
494.text: "I said: I don't want to talk about my family."

495.speaker: Walter Tusk
495.text: "I'm sorry, President. Let me know if I can help with anything."

498.speaker: Walter Tusk
498.text: "Nobody would want a son that steals your yacht and make the local news."

499.speaker: Mikail Aven
499.text: "Good news is that I finally convinced him to go to university. He will study economics in Lachaven Business School."

501.speaker: Walter Tusk
501.text: "Maybe your son will be a great future economist!"

503.speaker: Mikail Aven
503.text: "Not that I mean anything against you, Mr. Rayne."

505.speaker: Mikail Aven
505.text: "I'm very confident in your abilities to fix our recession."

507.speaker: Mikail Aven
507.text: "I hope we can repair the damages to our economy. We can't fail like Alphonso did."

513.speaker: Edith Agnoc
513.text: "Maybe you should help Mikail instead. I saw Darron made the local news with his yacht party in Benfi."

518.speaker: Narrator
518.text: Walter looked at the guards inside the room.

519.speaker: Walter Tusk
519.text: "A correction. It wasn't his policies that destroyed him."

521.speaker: Player
521.text: “I always had a bad feeling about his sudden fall.”

523.speaker: Walter Tusk
523.text: "Let's just say that he threatened the economic power base of some powerful figures within the government with his vast privatization plan. And they removed him."

530.speaker: Player
530.text: "You don't want to say this again in public."

532.speaker: Narrator
532.text: After a long silence, followed by some chit-chat, Walter ordered a bottle of whiskey.

533.speaker: Player
533.text: “Symon would you give a toast again?”

536.speaker: Narrator
536.text: The waiters brought one of the finest Arcasian whiskeys. It was time for a toast.

537.speaker: Player
537.text: “I raise to our health and happiness.”

540.speaker: Narrator
540.text: Edith stood up. Most of us were all a little tipsy at this point.

542.speaker: Narrator
542.text: The moon was shining bright as everyone except Walter left in their luxury cars.

543.speaker: Player
543.text: “It's getting late. Let's call it a night.”

548.speaker: Walter Tusk
548.text: “They say hope dies last, to the future.”

549.speaker: Symon Holl
549.text: “I think it's time we call it a night.”

550.speaker: Edith Agnoc
550.text: “I want to thank you, Mr. President for joining us and you Symon, for putting all this together.”

552.speaker: Symon Holl
552.text: “May the wheels of fortune always turn in our favour! The future of abundance awaits us!"

554.speaker: Edith Agnoc
554.text: “Good night everybody. It was a pleasure.”

555.speaker: Player
555.text: "Thank you Edith, for joining with a bunch of ugly rich men."

559.speaker: Narrator
559.text: Symon stood up. He seemed to have a slight issue with his balance.

560.speaker: Player
560.text: “To an equal society without class differences. A Morgna wes core!"

561.speaker: Narrator
561.text: Nobody else responded. And Symon looked like he had a little too much alcohol.

563.speaker: Narrator
563.text: There was an awkward silence as they looked at each other with glasses in their hands.

566.speaker: Walter Tusk
566.text: "Let's just drink this up and leave."

572.speaker: Narrator
572.text: After bidding our farewells, we slowly walked out the restaurant.

585.speaker: Walter Tusk
585.text: “You rejected our previous discrete offer to bail out businesses.”
585.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Relations_Walter_Promise_BailBusiness"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn01_InT_Investment_Highway"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn01_InT_Investment_Railway"] == true) == false)

589.speaker: Walter Tusk
589.text: “We had a deal about the business bailout package."
589.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Relations_Walter_Promise_BailBusiness"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn01_InT_Investment_Highway"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn01_InT_Investment_Railway"] == true) == false)

590.speaker: Walter Tusk
590.text: “You held on to that promise. This went well in our book.”

591.speaker: Walter Tusk
591.text: “This action led to disappointment in the Group.”

596.speaker: Walter Tusk
596.text: “However, you still made the right choice. Your party not getting that donation is unfortunate though. Why someone wouldn't want that money is beyond me.”

597.speaker: Walter Tusk
597.text: “You broke that promise. This action led to a huge disappointment in the Group.”

624.speaker: Edith Agnoc
624.text: "Oh. N-Nothing, Mr. President. I'm sorry if it came across wrong."

625.speaker: Narrator
625.text: The table went quiet for a few seconds.

626.speaker: Narrator
626.text: Walter stared at me as the guards bowed their heads and went outside.

630.speaker: Symon Holl
630.text: "I'd like to thank Mr. Rayne again for his decisiveness in office... I'm sure we will get through this emergency period and come out stronger."

637.speaker: Player
637.text: “I don't want to hear your comments, Mr. Tusk.”

639.speaker: Walter Tusk
639.text: “The comments of the Lotherberg Group should matter to you, President.”

645.speaker: Narrator
645.text: Everyone fell silent and looked at Mikail.

646.speaker: Walter Tusk
646.text: "Oh, excuse him, President! He didn't mean anything bad."

648.speaker: Narrator
648.text: Walter laughed and Mikail joined in with a nervous laughter soon after.

649.speaker: Edith Agnoc
649.text: “Enough with this Alphonso talk. His policies already destroyed him."

655.speaker: Player
655.text: "Looks like a cat caught our friend's tongue."

656.speaker: Mikail Aven
656.text: "No need to shout at the table, Mr. President."

658.speaker: Player
658.text: "You still didn't give me a response."

659.speaker: Mikail Aven
659.text: "I said 'Ewald Alphonso was the only leader who was well-versed in economics'. Please forgive me, I didn't mean to offend you."

661.speaker: Narrator
661.text: I stood up and left the room.

662.speaker: Narrator
662.text: Walter came running behind me as I walked outside.

666.speaker: Mikail Aven
666.text: "But I agree that we need more economists to enter politics. Thankfully we have a president who seems to be as well-versed in economics as Alphonso.”

667.speaker: Player
667.text: “I appreciate the advice but I don't like salmon."

671.speaker: Walter Tusk
671.text: "Ah, of course. Nobody can say no to a bottle of wine by Giralt of Ribery."
